YITA raises over RMB 100 million for force-controlled robot hardware

Seed and seed-plus funding includes Galbot and Fourier, supporting a focus on arms and joint modules for embodied AI.

TechNode ↗21 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Combined early-stage funding

Chinese robot hardware startup YITA disclosed on October 20 that it had raised over RMB 100 million across seed and seed-plus rounds, with TechNode reporting the following day. The figure combines two rounds rather than describing a separate new single-round investment.

Arms and joints for controlled contact

Founded in May 2026, YITA develops force-controlled arms and high-performance joint modules. Its portfolio spans integrated actuators, compliant dual-arm systems and manipulation platforms, targeting hardware that lets embodied AI and humanoid developers regulate contact forces when handling objects.

Investors and remaining unknowns

Named investors include Galbot, Fourier, Matrix Partners China, CCB International, SenseTime Guoxiang Capital and the L2F founder fund. Lighthouse Capital is its incubator and exclusive financial adviser. The report does not supply force-control accuracy, shipment figures or customer-test results establishing readiness across its portfolio.
